metaDescription: Six Honda two-stage gas snow blowers compared, from the 24-inch HSS724 to the 36-inch hybrid HSM1336i, with track and wheel drive explained.
expertTake: The HSS928 track-drive is the best all-round Honda for most large driveways, and the HSS724 is the right size for a typical suburban drive. The HSM1336i is for estates and commercial-style lots. If your driveway is short and paved, a Honda two-stage is more machine than you need.
introParagraphs: A premium gas two-stage machine is a purchase you expect to keep for a decade or more. The reason owners accept the higher entry cost is a commercial-grade engine, a drive system built to pull through heavy snow and a parts network that lasts.

The real choices inside one family come down to three things: how wide a path you need, whether wheels or tracks suit your surface, and how much engine you need for the depth and density of snow you actually get.

products.name: Honda HSS928AATD 28-inch two-stage, track drive, GX270
products.description:
The HSS928 is the middle of Honda's walk-behind range and, for most buyers, the right place to land. A commercial-grade GX270 overhead-valve engine drives a two-stage auger and impeller, with a 28-inch clearing path and a throw rated up to 52 feet.

Tracks are the reason to choose the AATD over a wheeled version. Rubber tracks spread the load, which helps on packed snow and on slopes where tires spin, and they hold a straight line at idle without the wheels walking sideways. Against the HSS724 you gain 4 inches of path and a bigger engine, and against the HSS1332 you save size and weight while still handling most residential storms.

Ownership is the old-school routine done properly. Fresh fuel with stabilizer, an oil change at the start of the season, a drive belt check and shear pins in the toolbox. Electric start removes the cold-morning pull cord, but a spare plug and a fuel shut-off that you use in spring are what keep the carburetor happy for years. If you only ever clear a short flat drive, this is more engine than you need; the value shows up on long runs, steep ramps and storms that drop a foot at a time.
products.bestFor: Larger residential drives that see deep, heavy snow and slopes.
pros: Track drive grips on packed snow and slopes
Commercial-grade GX270 engine
Up to 52 feet of throw
28-inch path trims passes on wide drives
cons: Heavy to load into a truck or step up a ramp
Premium purchase cost against off-brand 24-inch gas units

products.name: Honda HSS724AATD 23.8-inch two-stage, track drive, GX200
products.description:
The HSS724AATD is the smallest tracked Honda, with a 23.8-inch path and a GX200 engine. It still throws up to 49 feet, a figure close to the larger 28-inch model, which tells you the impeller design is where Honda put its effort.

Compared with the HSS928 it gives up 4 inches of path and about 400 pounds per minute of rated capacity. In exchange it is easier to maneuver on narrower drives and through gates. Tracks make it a good fit for owners with a slope, a steep gravel drive or an icy parking pad.

The lighter engine means less torque against compacted snow and berms, so expect slower travel through a plow bank. Upkeep is the same as any gas machine: fresh fuel, stabilizer before summer, oil change each year. The electric start is genuinely useful when the temperature drops. Its smaller engine also means lighter fuel use per hour, which matters if you clear for an hour or more every storm.
products.bestFor: Typical suburban drives with slopes or packed snow, where tracks help.
pros: Compact tracked footprint fits narrower drives
GX200 engine is a proven Honda design
Up to 49 feet of throw
Electric start for cold mornings
cons: Slower through plow berms than larger engines

products.name: Honda HSS724AAWD 23.8-inch two-stage, pneumatic tires
products.description:
The HSS724AAWD is the same 23.8-inch machine on 14-inch pneumatic tires rather than tracks. The engine, auger, impeller and 49-foot throw are unchanged, so the decision is purely about the drive system.

Wheels turn more easily, make the machine a little lighter to pivot and are cheaper to replace than tracks. They also work well on a flat, paved drive where grip is not an issue. The wheeled version is the better pick if you make many tight turns or have to move the machine across bare concrete.

On steep, icy or heavily packed surfaces the wheels slip sooner than tracks do, so the AATD wins there. Check tire pressure each season and fit chains if your drive is slick. If you choose this version, keep a set of tire chains in the garage; a slick driveway turns pneumatic tires into skates.
products.bestFor: Flat, paved drives where easy turning matters more than traction.
pros: Easier to pivot on bare pavement
Same GX200 engine and throw as the track model
Pneumatic tires cost less to replace than tracks
Electric start included
cons: Tires slip sooner on ice and slopes
Tire pressure and chains are another upkeep item

products.name: Honda HSS1332AATD 31.9-inch two-stage, track drive, GX390
products.description:
The HSS1332 is the large-lot model, a 31.9-inch path with a GX390 engine and a rated 2,750 pounds per minute. Its throw reaches 56 feet, which is useful when the plow bank is far from the drive edge.

Against the HSS928 it brings 3.9 inches more width and a bigger engine, and against the HSM1336i it is the more conventional design with a slightly smaller path. Tracks, electric start and a heavy chassis make it a serious tool for deep drifts.

It is also a heavy machine, so check your ramp or loading plan before you buy. Treat the fuel carefully, drain the carburetor or add stabilizer before summer and replace shear pins and belts on schedule. It is overkill for a short drive. Plan the storage spot first: at this size it takes the corner of a two-car garage, and the track footprint is wider than a typical walk-behind.
products.bestFor: Large lots, long lanes and heavy, wind-packed drifts.
pros: Wide 31.9-inch path for fewer passes
GX390 engine rated for 2,750 lb per minute
Throw up to 56 feet
Track drive for traction
cons: Very heavy and bulky to store
More machine than a normal driveway needs

products.name: Honda HSS1332APT 31.9-inch two-stage, track drive, GX390
products.description:
The HSS1332APT shares the HSS1332's engine, 31.9-inch path and 56-foot throw. The listing highlights track drive and auger height adjustment, which helps when you switch between a bare drive and a gravel one.

As a variant of the AATD above it, the engine and capacity do not change, so decide on features and availability. If you need the control layout and drive described in the listing, this version fits; otherwise choose the AATD and compare what each listing includes.

Ownership is the same as for the AATD. Use fresh fuel, change oil each season and confirm the controls match your hands before buying, since this machine is a big investment. Read both listings line by line and compare what is in the box, because the two version codes can differ in details that matter more than the engine.
products.bestFor: Large lots where the auger height adjustment on the listing is a requirement.
pros: Same GX390 engine as the other HSS1332
56-foot throw clears banks far from the drive
Track drive grips on slopes
Wide 31.9-inch path
cons: Same weight and size as the AATD
Features overlap heavily with the AATD version

products.name: Honda HSM1336i 36-inch two-stage, track drive, iGX390
products.description:
The HSM1336i is Honda's widest machine, with a 36-inch path, an iGX390 engine and a rated throw of 62.3 feet. The hybrid design uses the engine to power the auger and impeller and separate electric drive for the tracks, which is why the listing describes smoother go and better throw.

Compared with the HSS1332 it adds 4 inches of path and about 250 pounds per minute of capacity, and it moves the travel drive to an electric system for smoother speed control. That makes it a very capable machine for estates, school lots and long private roads.

It is a heavy investment, and the hybrid components add a new layer to repairs, so choose it only if you need that width. A smaller Honda or a different brand will serve most homeowners better. Hybrid models also change what a service call involves, so ask your local dealer whether they stock parts for the electric drive before you commit.
products.bestFor: Estates and large lots needing the widest path and longest throw.
pros: 36-inch path, the widest in this lineup
Hybrid system gives smooth drive speed
Up to 62.3 feet of throw
Rated up to 3,000 lb per minute
cons: Large and heavy for most residential garages

buyingCriteria.explanation: Honda's rated capacity runs from 1,500 pounds per minute on the GX200-powered HSS724 to 2,750 on the GX390 HSS1332 and 3,000 on the HSM1336i. The figure tells you how fast the machine can chew through density. A buyer with a short drive in wet snow does not need 3,000, but a long lane with plow berms might. Match engine to the heaviest snow you routinely face. A short wet-snow drive in a mild climate gets nothing from the extra pounds per minute, while a long lane in lake-effect country will use all of them.

Rubber tracks spread the load and hold traction on ice, slopes and packed snow, which is why most Honda models here use them. The wheeled HSS724AAWD uses 14-inch pneumatic tires, which turn more easily on bare pavement but slip sooner on ice. Choose tracks for slopes and gravel, wheels for flat paved drives.

Width from 23.8 to 36 inches changes the number of passes. A 28-inch HSS928 takes about 15 percent fewer passes than a 23.8-inch HSS724 on the same drive. Wider machines are harder to store and to steer through gates. Measure your narrowest gate or path before buying; a wider chassis that will not fit through the side yard is a daily irritation.

Honda quotes 49 feet for the HSS724, 52 for the HSS928, 56 for the HSS1332 and 62.3 for the HSM1336i. Throw matters when your plow bank is far from the drive edge or when the wind blows snow back at you. A longer throw also costs weight and engine power.

Track-drive Hondas in this width class are heavy, and the largest ones need a ramp or a helper to move. Check your garage floor and steps. If you cannot load it, you cannot service it or take it for repair.

These engines are available with commercial-grade parts, and Honda dealers are common. That is a real advantage over generic imports, since shear pins, belts, scrapers and skid shoes are stocked locally. Factor the service network into cost. Dealers who service Honda engines often stock belts, shear pins and scrapers, which means a Saturday repair instead of a week of waiting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Engine and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked the lineup by engine family and stated pounds-per-minute capacity, from the GX200 at 1,500 up to the iGX390 at 3,000. We read these as relative figures, not guarantees. We also noted that the HSS724 and HSS928 use different engine families, so their gap is bigger than the path width suggests.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive system
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared track and wheeled variants because surface and slope decide which one wins. We noted that the HSS724 is the only model here offered on pneumatic tires.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at clearing width from 23.8 to 36 inches and treated the heavier machines as a storage and loading cost. Based on the spec sheet, a bigger path always means a heavier chassis.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered upkeep that gas machines demand: fuel stabilizer, oil changes, belts, shear pins and carburetor care. Honda's parts network is a plus; the hybrid HSM1336i adds electronics. A machine that is expensive to fix is not worth much if parts take a month to arrive.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit to driveway
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each model to a driveway length and snow type rather than naming a winner overall. This is an editorial assessment, not a measured score.

rows: More power and width with tracks
Adds tracks to the same engine

cards.label: Tracks
cards.text: The HSS724AATD, HSS928, HSS1332 and HSM1336i use rubber tracks that spread weight and grip on packed snow and slopes. They hold a line and cost more to repair.

cards.label: Wheels
cards.text: The HSS724AAWD uses 14-inch pneumatic tires. They are easier to pivot and cheaper to replace, but slip on ice and steep drives.

howToChoose.note: Choose tracks for slopes and gravel; wheels suit flat paved drives.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Tracks and enough engine to climb without the auger bogging. Weight helps traction but also adds momentum on the way down.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Honda HSS928AATD is the most balanced tracked pick. Wheeled models like the HSS724AAWD slip first on grades.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long drive, steep grade or lake-effect snow. The HSS928 or HSS1332 will save time on every storm.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a short flat drive. The HSS724 is already generous, and a smaller brand or battery machine may be enough.

maintenance.why: Cold oil thickens and starves the engine of lubrication. Fresh oil protects bearings in sub-zero starts.
Stale fuel gums carburetors. Use stabilizer or run the tank dry before summer storage.
Shear pins protect the gearbox, and belts slip when worn. Carry spares of both. Spare pins cost little and save a trip to the dealer in the middle of a storm.
Track tension or tire pressure affects traction. Replace worn cleats before they fail.
A fresh plug makes cold starts easier. Keep a spare in the toolbox.

faq.q: Are Honda snow blowers worth the price?
faq.a: They cost more than imported gas units, mainly for commercial-grade engines and parts support. If you keep the machine for ten or more seasons, the longevity can justify it. For a short drive, a cheaper unit does the job. Resale value on these machines also tends to hold up better than generic brands.

faq.q: Tracks or wheels on a Honda?
faq.a: Tracks are better on slopes, ice and packed snow. Wheels pivot more easily on flat pavement and cost less to replace. Choose based on surface and slope.

faq.q: Which Honda suits a three-car driveway?
faq.a: The HSS724 handles it comfortably. Step up to the HSS928 if you get heavy snow or a long approach. A two-car drive is easily within the HSS724 as well.

faq.q: What does the iGX390 hybrid do?
faq.a: It runs the auger and impeller from the engine and drives the tracks electrically. That gives smoother speed control but adds electronics to maintain.
Electric start is a real help in deep cold when a pull cord is hard to use. All the models here have it.

faq.q: How do I store it for summer?
faq.a: Drain the fuel or add stabilizer, change the oil and clean the housing. A dry spot prevents rust on the auger and chute. Also remove the shear pins and lubricate the auger shaft so everything moves freely next season.
